issues.description: The problem specification and UML require a static method named acceptSupplyDelivery(String, int, int) to add deliveries to the shared stock. The provided solution implements an equivalent static method but names it receiveDelivery(String, int, int) instead. The template's (commented) Main and the problem text expect acceptSupplyDelivery, so this name mismatch creates a structural/signature inconsistency that will confuse students and break code/tests relying on the expected method name.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the solution method receiveDelivery to acceptSupplyDelivery with the same parameters (String name, int price, int quantity), or add a static acceptSupplyDelivery wrapper that delegates to receiveDelivery. Ensure the method name matches the UML/problem statement so students and tests can call acceptSupplyDelivery as specified.

issues.description: The problem statement specifies a static method named acceptSupplyDelivery(String, int, int) for SealSaloon, but the solution implementation provides a static method named receiveDelivery(String, int, int). The project Main (both template and solution) still refers to acceptSupplyDelivery. This creates a direct naming mismatch for the same conceptual operation (receiving a supply delivery) across the problem text, example usage, and the solution, making it unclear which method name students should implement or call.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the method name across all artifacts. Rename the solution method receiveDelivery(...) to acceptSupplyDelivery(...) (keeping it static and with the same parameters), and update any references (including Main) accordingly. Alternatively, update the problem statement and example usage to refer to receiveDelivery if that name is preferred — but ensure the name is consistent between the problem, template examples, and the solution implementation.
